embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: All six main actors have visually separate bodies and tools; the jackal and ibis are role masks over continuous adult torsos, and the three Fate hand pairs remain attached to their respective actors.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: Anubis reaches the scale adjustment, Thoth reaches the tablet, and all three seated Fates reach their local reel, rod, or scissors through connected visible arms.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: Seated Fates are supported at the foreground bench; standing roles rest on the stage. The scale’s center pedestal supports the horizontal beam and both hanging pans.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: The scissors do not establish the requested fresh cut on the horizontal strand, and Clotho’s visible reel lacks the intended flax-to-spindle contact. The same life-thread never meets the deceased woman’s medallion.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: The pen tip at the tablet edge and the heart’s matching owner mark are hidden or absent; the thread exits right rather than showing its intended contact with the woman. These consequential relations cannot be assessed.

supplemental_observations.impression: A rich staged mythic tableau with a still central adult woman, a legible scale judgment group, and a foreground Fate mechanism. The installed-tree idea became a scenic painted/digital panorama rather than a clearly physical sculptural installation.
strengths: Same two-pan heart-feather scale and visible admission arch.
Foreground measuring action and broad tree tier hierarchy.
weaknesses: The three Fate roles read mostly through tools rather than all intended mechanisms.
Spinning, fresh severance, and final same-soul thread ownership are missing.
Thoth’s writing contact and heart’s shared cartouche are not assessable.
